_description: Frontend / UI decisions: visual system, palette, theming, wizard structure. Append only; supersede with a new entry instead of editing.

title: Game Boy pixel-art 1-bit aesthetic with CRT overlay
context: Need a distinctive visual identity that matches the tabletop RPG theme. Alternatives considered: modern flat UI; dark fantasy theme; Material Design.
decision: Adopt a Game Boy 1-bit aesthetic with a 4-shade palette and a viewport-level CRT scanline overlay.
rationale: Distinctive retro feel that matches the tabletop RPG theme. 4-shade palette is simple to implement and creates strong visual identity.
consequences_positive: Unique visual identity; palette system allows genre-based theming

title: Genre-based dynamic palette system
context: Want visual variety across genres without redesigning components. Alternatives considered: single fixed palette; user-chosen theme.
decision: Each genre family ships its own 4-shade palette; the active palette switches based on the user's genre selection.
rationale: Each genre combination shifts the 4-shade palette. A cyberpunk campaign looks different from a dark fantasy one, creating visual variety without redesigning components.
consequences_positive: 6 genre-specific palettes implemented, auto-switching based on selection

title: Tailwind v4 with @theme for CSS variable overrides
context: Tailwind v4 changed the override mechanism away from :root. Alternative considered: :root CSS custom properties (Tailwind v3 pattern).
decision: All CSS variable overrides live in @theme blocks (or @layer theme { .light { } } for Nuxt UI vars), never :root.
rationale: Tailwind v4 moved to @theme blocks instead of :root. Using :root would not work correctly with Tailwind's theme resolution.
consequences_positive: Correct integration with Tailwind v4 theme system

title: i18n strings use natural case; uppercase applied via CSS
context: Storing uppercase in locale files reduces flexibility. Alternative considered: store uppercase strings in locale files.
decision: Locale files keep natural case; visual uppercase uses CSS text-transform.
rationale: Storing uppercase in locale files makes them harder to reuse in different contexts. CSS text-transform is the correct layer for visual presentation.
consequences_positive: Flexible text that can be styled differently per context

title: 4-step wizard with genre-based carousel and cartridge slot UI
context: Original genre selector was a checkbox grid; UX was flat. Alternatives considered: simple checkbox grid; dropdown selection.
decision: Genre selection is a sidebar + carousel UI with a Game Boy cartridge metaphor.
rationale: Redesigned genre selection from simple checkboxes to a sidebar + carousel UI for better UX. Cartridge metaphor fits the Game Boy aesthetic.
consequences_positive: More engaging and thematic genre selection experience

title: CRT scanline overlay applied at viewport root, not on individual components
context: Per-component overlays caused z-index conflicts. Alternatives considered: per-component overlay; CSS filter on root element.
decision: A single overlay div covers the full viewport; no component-level scanline code.
rationale: Scanlines are a screen-level effect — applying per-component creates z-index conflicts and inconsistent rendering when components overlap or scroll.
consequences_positive: Single overlay div covers the full viewport uniformly; no component-level overlay code

title: Wizard as the main app shell instead of separate pages per step
context: Generation state must persist across step transitions. Alternatives considered: separate route per step; modal flow.
decision: WizardStepper is the app shell; Pinia owns wizard state across steps.
rationale: Generation state must survive step transitions — characters must still be visible when the user navigates to the script step. Separate pages would reset state or require complex URL-based persistence.
consequences_positive: Pinia store persists state across steps; wizard navigation is instant with no page reload
